title: Stakeholder Signal Artifactization and Priority Commit Protocol
creator: Leah Patel
description:
Problem: Top-account requests and executive escalations currently arrive as disparate signals (emails, CSM notes, Zendesk threads, sales decks) and are inconsistently translated into prioritizable roadmap inputs. This leads to ad-hoc commitments, misaligned expectations, and difficulty measuring when an ask should displace planned work.

Goal: Build a repeatable process and light tooling to convert stakeholder signals into structured artifacts (use case brief, acceptance criteria, severity/context tags, eval prompt set) and apply a transparent Priority Commit Protocol (PCP) that produces a binding, timeboxed commitment or a documented deferral with reason. The protocol should be operable without heavy manual overhead and integrate with existing intake and SLO gates.

Scope: Prototype the artifact schema, scorecard, and handoff flow for top-50 accounts and escalations. Integrate with CSM intake, Sales Ops, and Support triage. Build a small intake form and a Google Sheet + Linear templates for initial rollouts. Plan automation hooks in Q2 to feed structured signals into the roadmap engine.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact schema defined and reviewed by PM, Design, and Solutions Engineering
PCP scorecard (quantitative + qualitative) documented and decision thresholds agreed
Pilot intake form implemented and used by CSMs for at least 12 requests from top-50 accounts
Three end-to-end mock escalations executed: intake -> scoring -> commit/deferral -> stakeholder comms
Linear templates created for auto-populating tickets with artifact fields and expected SLA
Stakeholder-facing commit message template and rollback triggers agreed and stored in Confluence
decisions: Use lightweight artifact schema (one page) rather than full PRD to keep cycle fast
Scorecard will combine business impact (ARR at risk), product fit, engineering cost, and regulatory need with a decay factor for stale signals
Initial commitments are timeboxed 'micro-commits' (4-6 week delivery windows) to avoid long-term scope lock
Automation will be phased: start manual + sheet, progress to Slack + webhook, then integrate with roadmap engine
notes: Trade-offs: faster intake means lower granularity of requirements; mitigated by requiring eval prompts for high-risk asks
Design input: prefer a short form with progressive disclosure to avoid CSM friction
Legal/Compliance: flagged asks requiring data residency/privacy checks will automatically route to Private deploy PMs
updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff w/ CSM, Sales Ops, Solutions Eng. Agreed on top-50 account pilot and owner matrix.
2025-02-20: Draft artifact schema posted to Confluence; request feedback from Eng leads by 2025-02-27.
2025-02-27: Engineering feedback: propose 'eval prompt set' as required field when customer_impact=high. Adding to ACs.
2025-02-28: Design mocked a one-page intake form; UX review scheduled 2025-03-03.
2025-03-01: Decided on micro-commit windows for initial pilot and to lock acceptance criteria at commit time. Assigned owners for pilot tracking sheet.
